1.explanation:
• PaletteTexture.js—manages the 1D lookup texture for palette styles. If its texture isn’t deleted or rebound to the new context on layer re‐add, the old GL texture handle becomes invalid.
• TileTexture.js—wraps each tile’s RGBA WebGL texture. Without proper disposal and recreation when the layer’s context is lost, black tiles appear.
• BaseTileRepresentation.js—coordinates the creation and caching of TileTexture/PaletteTexture per tile. It needs to listen for context‐loss or layer removal to destroy stale textures.
• styleparser.js—generates GLSL shader code for palette styles. If shader programs aren’t recompiled after context recreation, they will reference invalid textures.
• renderer/webgl/TileLayerBase.js & TileLayer.js—set up and manage the WebGL tile layer pipeline, including initializing representations. They must tear down and reinitialize the BaseTileRepresentation when the layer is removed and re‐added, but currently do not, leading to stale resources being reused.
1.bug_scenario: A WebGLTileLayer styled with a palette renders correctly on first addition, but after calling map.removeLayer(layer) and then map.addLayer(layer) again, the layer comes back as a solid black tile and the console shows WebGL warnings about binding textures from a lost or different context. In other words, palette‐based tile textures or associated shader resources aren’t being cleaned up or re‐initialized when the layer’s WebGL context is torn down and recreated.

2.explanation:
• src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js – defines the WebGLTileLayer and kicks off style parsing and representation creation when the layer is added
• src/ol/webgl/styleparser.js – extracts palette stops from the style expression and drives creation of the palette texture
• src/ol/webgl/PaletteTexture.js – creates and uploads the palette color lookup texture to the GL context; if not re-created on re-add, it points at an invalid context
• src/ol/webgl/TileTexture.js & BaseTileRepresentation.js – manage the tile and palette texture references and uniforms for each tile; stale references here lead to binding textures from the wrong context
• src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js & TileLayerBase.js – orchestrate rendering of WebGLTileLayers, including context loss/restore handling and resource cleanup; missing or incomplete cleanup/re-initialization of palette textures here causes the black tiles and context-mismatch errors
2.bug_scenario: A WebGLTileLayer styled with a palette renders correctly on first add, but after calling map.removeLayer(layer) and map.addLayer(layer) several times, the tiles go black. The browser console reports WebGL warnings like "bindTexture: tex is from a different (or lost) WebGL context." This indicates that the palette texture (and possibly other WebGL resources) created for the layer aren’t being re-initialized or rebound to the current WebGL context when the layer is re-added.
